items.claim: The rear seam at web:Isa.53.9|web:Isa.53.10 is cut across a byte-identical verbal device that the row never discloses, and two of its supporting citations do not match the bytes they gloss.
items.evidence: All three pointed splices reach byte tier at their cited verses (oshb:Isa.53.1, oshb:Isa.53.6, oshb:Isa.53.10), and the fronted divine-name clause opening oshb:Isa.53.10 is byte-true and verse-initial, so the seam is not baseless. But a byte-true device straddles it undisclosed: the form נָשָׂ֔א stands at MT 53:4, inside this row, and נָשָׂ֔א at MT 53:12, outside it, and at byte tier that form occurs in exactly TWO verses of the book (sweep: 2 verses, MT 53:4 and MT 53:12; accent-stripped 6, consonantal 39) — the only byte-identical pair of that form in the book, bracketing this row's own rear seam. Two further root pairs bracket it at consonantal tier: סְבָלָ֑ם (MT 53:4) with יִסְבֹּֽל (MT 53:11), and הִפְגִּ֣יעַ (MT 53:6) with יַפְגִּֽיעַ (MT 53:12). The row's rival is argued from a shared grammatical subject and from the English, never from these forms, so the continuity case the bytes actually make is not answered. Second, the pointed splice cited at oshb:Isa.53.6 is כֻּלָּ֨נוּ֙, the verse-INITIAL token, but the gloss attached to it is the closing clause of that verse, whose form is the distinct כֻּלָּֽנוּ — the two are different byte forms in one verse, and the quote and its gloss do not line up. Third, the rival sentence turns on 'the earlier portion of' web:Isa.53.11, but the two staged witnesses diverge exactly there: the WEB rendering there carries a light-seeing clause with no counterpart token in that verse's MT bytes (MT 53:11 runs from the toil-of-his-soul phrase straight to the satisfaction verb). A rival keyed to a WEB half-verse over a divergence, with no pointed splice, is translation-dependent. The servant possessive it names is likewise asserted without a quoted form. Mark discipline is clean: across the 9 verses MT 53:1-9 the single-witness layers stand at 0 parashah segs, 0 paseq segs and 0 ketiv/qere notes, so nothing is owed under span-relevant symmetry, and the row correctly claims none. The referent is not decided.

items.claim: The seam and the mark disclosure hold up in the bytes, but the row's servant-recurrence claim is neither quoted nor tier-labelled and is not byte-true, and the same undisclosed byte device straddles this row's front seam.
items.evidence: Both pointed splices reach byte tier at oshb:Isa.53.10 and oshb:Isa.53.12 and both sit verse-initially, as claimed; the subject-fronted divine name genuinely opens MT 53:10. The setumah claim is correct in type and location — MT 53:12 carries a SAMEKH seg — the span's one parashah seg (1 marked verse across the 3 verses MT 53:10-12) — with no petuchah conflated, and 0 paseq segs and 0 ketiv/qere notes across those 3 verses, so symmetry is complete. The defect is the recurrence claim: the row ties the divine possessive opening web:Isa.52.13 to its recurrence inside web:Isa.53.11 without quoting either form and without naming a tier. The forms are עַבְדִּ֑י (MT 52:13) and עַבְדִּ֖י (MT 53:11) — they differ in the bytes and match only once accents are stripped, so an unqualified 'recurs' overstates by one tier on the claim that carries the row's held-referent reasoning. Second, the byte-identical pair spanning MT 53:4 and MT 53:12 straddles this row's FRONT seam from the other side: נָשָׂ֔א at MT 53:12, inside this row, is byte-identical to נָשָׂ֔א at MT 53:4, outside it, and those are the only two byte-tier occurrences in the book (sweep: 2 verses) — continuity evidence at the seam the row opens on, undisclosed here as well. The referent is correctly left undecided, and no cross-tradition material is used.

items.claim: The row's load-bearing evidence — a five-site set of 'says Yahweh'/'declares Yahweh' signatures — is a blended sweep across three distinct byte objects with no pointed splice anywhere, and one member is not a Yahweh signature at all in either witness.
items.evidence: The five cited signature sites resolve in the bytes into three separate objects and four separate shapes, with zero of the five quoted. MT 54:1 ends אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה — that exact pointed run occurs at byte tier in 5 verses of the book (sweep: 5 verses, MT 39:6, 54:1, 65:25, 66:21, 66:23) and at NONE of MT 54:6, 54:8, 54:10, 54:17. MT 54:6 ends אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ: the divine element is the suffixed God-noun, not the tetragrammaton, and the row's own cited translation reads “says your God” (web:Isa.54.6) — this is the separate variant that the divine-speech count-object expressly excludes, so citing it as a Yahweh signature blends two count-objects. MT 54:8 ends אָמַ֥ר גֹּאֲלֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה and MT 54:10 ends אָמַ֥ר מְרַחֲמֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה: both interpose a participial epithet, so neither is the adjacent formula either. MT 54:17 ends נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, which belongs to the postpositive oracle-signature census — a different formula entirely, bracketed here with the speaking verb under one label. The set is the ground both for keeping the chapter whole and for rejecting the finer cut, so the blend is load-bearing, not incidental. Second, the universal 'no fresh addressee or scene shift interrupts the sustained address across the chapter' is contested inside the span. This row's own front-seam warrant is רָנִּ֥י עֲקָרָ֖ה לֹ֣א יָלָ֑דָה (MT 54:1); MT 54:11 opens עֲנִיָּ֥ה סֹעֲרָ֖ה לֹ֣א נֻחָ֑מָה — the same three-part shape with the same accentual contour, and the pivot token לֹ֣א is byte-identical at both verses. An internal onset built on the identical shape as the seam warrant is undisclosed. Third, span-relevant mark symmetry is incomplete: the three SAMEKH segs at MT 54:8, 54:10 and 54:17 are correct and complete, and the ketiv/qere at MT 54:16 is described exactly right — unpointed הן running into pointed הִנֵּ֤ה as a doubled token pair — but MT 54:2 carries a paseq seg inside this row's span that the row never discloses, while the parallel seg at MT 56:4 is disclosed where it occurs. Fourth, the cross-seam title claim is called byte-true but is unquoted and untiered, and the two instances are not byte-identical: קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (MT 54:5) against the prefixed וְלִקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (MT 55:5) — the shared run reaches accent-stripped tier only. Finally, the span's last verse carries עַבְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֧ה (consonantal sweep: 1 verse, MT 54:17), the PLURAL servants-of-Yahweh, immediately after two rows built on the singular possessive; the row engages no servant object at all. Minor: the front splice is cut mid-clause at the negative particle, stopping one token short of the verb that defines the addressee — and short of the very token that recurs at MT 54:11.

items.claim: The front seam is byte-solid and the invitation role-split is exactly right, but the row's declared driver is addressee shift while an undisclosed addressee-number shift sits inside its own span, and its rear-seam warrant does not discriminate in the bytes.
items.evidence: Credit where due: ה֤וֹי כָּל צָמֵא֙ is byte tier at oshb:Isa.55.1 and verse-initial, and the row names the role correctly — the invitation cry, not a woe-oracle onset, not the divine self-exclamation, and the contained different-lexeme woe form is not blended in. Mark discipline is complete: SAMEKH at MT 55:5 in-span and MT 54:17 at the front seam, tier-3 single-witness, with 0 paseq segs and 0 ketiv/qere notes across the 5 verses MT 55:1-5. The first defect is an addressee-number shift the row's own driver should have caught and the English cannot see. MT 55:1-3 address a masculine PLURAL throughout — אָזְנְכֶם֙ and נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם at MT 55:3, with the plural imperative chain — MT 55:4 carries no addressee at all, and MT 55:5 turns to masculine SINGULAR across the whole verse — the verb תֵדַע֙ early in the verse, then the God-noun אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ and the closing verb פֵאֲרָֽךְ. Singular-you suffixes appear in 1 of the 7 verses MT 55:1-7, and MT 55:5 is that verse. Both witnesses render every one of these with the same undifferentiated English pronoun, so the shift exists only in the Hebrew; a row driven by addressee shift that ends on the one verse where the addressee changes number owes that disclosure. The second defect is the rear-seam warrant. 'A further imperative opens web:Isa.55.6' does not discriminate: דִּרְשׁ֥וּ at MT 55:6 is the same masculine-plural imperative class already running through this row's own span — לְכ֣וּ at MT 55:1 is byte-identical to the same form at MT 55:3, alongside הַטּ֤וּ and שִׁמְע֖וּ. What changes at MT 55:6 is the imperative's object, not its form-class. With the form claim neutralised, the seam rests on a tier-3 single-witness seg that can never be a driver. Third, the cross-seam title disclosure is unquoted and untiered on both sides: the MT 55:5 form וְלִקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל is prefixed and is not byte-identical to קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל at MT 54:5 (accent-stripped tier).
tier_citations: tier-3 single-witness parashah: SAMEKH at MT 55:5, MT 54:17
single-witness mark layer: MT 55:1-5 no paseq, no K/Q

items.claim: The row walls its rear seam off from texture argument while a byte-identical run straddles that very seam undisclosed, and its front-seam warrant repeats the non-discriminating imperative claim used at the web:Isa.55.5|web:Isa.55.6 seam.
items.evidence: Credit where due: both pointed splices reach byte tier at oshb:Isa.55.6 and oshb:Isa.55.8; the postpositive signature claim is byte-accurate, with נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה standing verse-final at MT 55:8 (that pointed run is byte tier in exactly 2 verses, sweep: 2 verses, MT 55:8 and MT 59:20); the ketiv/qere at MT 55:13 is described exactly right — unpointed תחת running immediately into the pointed conjunction-prefixed וְתַ֥חַת in the source bytes; and the parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 55:13 in-span and MT 55:5 at the front seam), with 0 paseq segs across the 8 verses MT 55:6-13. The defect is the rear seam. The row declares it non-negotiable independent of any internal-texture argument — and a byte-true device straddles it: לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת closes MT 55:13, this row's final verse, and לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת closes MT 56:5, three verses past the seam, BYTE-IDENTICAL. The consonantal skeleton of that pair occurs in exactly 3 verses of the book (sweep: 3 verses, MT 48:19, 55:13, 56:5), so the pairing across the seam is not incidental, and it comes doubled: לְא֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ם at MT 55:13 against שֵׁ֤ם עוֹלָם֙ at MT 56:5. Declaring a seam immune to texture argument is precisely the move that cross-seam disclosure exists to prevent; the device may not move the seam, but it must be answered, not exempted. Second, the front-seam warrant repeats the weakness of the warrant used at the web:Isa.55.5|web:Isa.55.6 seam: דִּרְשׁ֥וּ is the same masculine-plural imperative class already running in MT 55:1-3, so 'a further imperative distinguishable from the invitation cry' is not a form-class change in the bytes.

single-witness mark layer: MT 55:6-13 no paseq

items.claim: The row asserts that its governing frame recurs verbatim at byte tier between its two cited verses, and the bytes refuse it — the two forms differ in pointing, not merely accents, and reach only consonantal tier against each other.
items.evidence: The row's own splice כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (MT 56:1, byte tier at its cited verse) re-checks against MT 56:4 at CONSONANTAL tier only, in both directions; it fails even the accent-stripped tier, because the divergence is in the pointing: the opening letter carries a dagesh at MT 56:1 and none at MT 56:4, whose form is כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה, subordinated by the preceding conjunction כִּי rather than standing verse-initial as at MT 56:1. 'Recurs verbatim at byte tier' is therefore false as written, and it is the row's stated ground for holding the whole span as one admission unit. Second, a position claim the bytes contradict: the row says it closes on the postpositive signature and that the formula seals the promise expressed in the clause it quotes. In MT 56:8 that run — נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה — is verse-INITIAL: it heads the verse and introduces the gathering clause it is said to seal, and both staged witnesses put the formula ahead of that speech. The formula class is postpositive book-wide; this instance is not. Third, this row's front seam carries the undisclosed byte-identical closing run shared by MT 55:13 and MT 56:5 (sweep: 3 verses at consonantal tier, MT 48:19, 55:13, 56:5). Against all that, the unity the row wants is byte-provable and unused: שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ at MT 56:2 is BYTE-IDENTICAL to שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ at MT 56:6 (sweep: 2 verses, the only two in the book), and וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי at MT 56:4 is byte-identical to וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי at MT 56:6 — a byte refrain pair bracketing the third-person turn the row is arguing across. Credit where due: frame ownership is correct — both cited frame verses sit on the divine side of the census, and the four royal-messenger sites are correctly confined to the narrative zone; the divine-name object at MT 56:8 is correctly named as the stacked adonai-plus-tetragrammaton form rather than the bare title; and the mark handling is exact — three in-span SAMEKH segs plus the front-seam seg, petuchah never conflated, the MT 56:4 paseq disclosed count-only with no intra-verse position claimed, and 0 ketiv/qere notes across the 8 verses MT 56:1-8.

items.claim: The row's front-boundary warrant carries no Hebrew at all, and the bytes contest it twice — the imperative is not verse-initial, and the same form recurs inside the row's own span in a different speech-role, undisclosed.
items.evidence: The opening seam is argued entirely from the English rendering; no pointed splice supports it, and it is the claim the row leans on hardest. In the bytes MT 56:9 opens כֹּ֖ל חַיְת֣וֹ שָׂדָ֑י — a vocative noun phrase standing first under a disjunctive accent — with the imperative אֵתָ֕יוּ following it, so 'the imperative summons opens this row' misplaces the form. Worse, that same imperative recurs verse-initially at MT 56:12, three verses later and INSIDE this row's span, as the scoffers' own quoted speech: אֵתָ֥יוּ, accent-stripped-identical to the MT 56:9 form (consonantal sweep: 12 verses book-wide, two of them MT 56:9 and MT 56:12). A form used as the row's boundary device and reappearing within the span in the opposite speech-role owes a role-split disclosure before it can carry a seam; the row instead states that no frame marker intervenes at MT 56:12 while its own opening device stands there. Quote-and-gloss parity slips once: the pointed splice at oshb:Isa.56.10 runs from כֻּלָּם֙, but the gloss attached covers only the mute-dogs clause and drops the quantifier the splice includes. Credit is substantial elsewhere. Both splices reach byte tier at their cited verses. The ketiv/qere handling at MT 56:10 is exactly right and demonstrably so: the verse opens with unpointed צפו immediately followed by pointed צֹפָ֞יו, and the row's splice does begin after that varying pair. The negative mark claim checks out — MT 56:8 carries 0 segs of any layer — and the SAMEKH at MT 56:9 is the span's one parashah seg (1 marked verse across the 6 verses MT 56:9-57:2), with 0 paseq segs present, so symmetry is complete. The rear boundary is byte-solid: MT 57:3 opens וְאַתֶּ֥ם קִרְבוּ הֵ֖נָּה, a fronted independent pronoun plus imperative plus vocative, which the row's own reading of MT 57:1-2 as a register shift rather than a new address respects. And the internal cohesion the row wants is byte-real though unused: כֻּלָּם֙ at MT 56:10 is byte-identical to the same form at MT 56:11. No language-zone claim is attached to that imperative form, correctly.
